## Findings
- claim-1: \(\Lambda/I_{6,5}\) has Schur basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq5^6\}\), and multiplication is LR multiplication with terms outside \(5^6\) discarded. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- claim-2: With \(A_+:=\bigoplus_{e>0}A_e\) and \(\bar h_t=\bar s_{(t)}\), one has \(A_+=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5)\).
- claim-3: Put \[ C_d=\{\mu:22\subseteq\mu\subseteq5^6,\ |\mu|=d\},\qquad R_d=\{(t,\lambda):1\le t\le5,\ 22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6,\ |\lambda|=d-t\}. \] The row indexed by \((t,\lambda)\in R_d\), in the basis \(C_d\), is \[ \bar h_t\bar s_\lambda =\sum_{\substack{\mu\in C_d\\\mu/\lambda\text{ horizontal }t\text{-strip}}}\bar s_\mu, \] and the lattice spanned by all these rows is exactly \((A_+J)_d\).
- claim-4: \(R_d=\varnothing\) for \(d\le4\) (hence for \(d<4\)) and for \(d>35\). For every \(31\le d\le35\), \(R_d\ne\varnothing\), since \((d-30,5^6)\in R_d\), but every indexed row is the zero vector because \(C_d=\varnothing\).
- claim-5: The supplied record identifies artifact `a3ad933b835c991bc8edccec918dce17c0e4594e4d1d4281e32946dd7e508ece` only as having been executed in degrees \(4,\ldots,30\); it supplies neither its degree-\(31,\ldots,35\) matrices nor its executable row-label data. Thus literal all-degree equality with that physical artifact’s indexed rows is not evidenced. [artifact 7407218a74525cf0e95adab0a2768940ab22d2e9faa3a3ddb10e5189643c306c, L1-L89]
## Strategy
Let \(\bar h_t=\bar s_{(t)}\) and \(A_+=\bigoplus_{e>0}A_e\). Jacobi–Trudi gives \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\); since \(\bar h_t=0\) for \(t>5\), homogeneity gives
\[
A_+=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5).
\]
Using truncated LR multiplication [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-269],
\[
(A_+J)_d=\sum_{t=1}^5\sum_{\substack{22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6\\|\lambda|=d-t}}
\mathbb Z\,\bar h_t\bar s_\lambda .
\]
For
\[
C_d=\{\mu:22\subseteq\mu\subseteq5^6,\ |\mu|=d\},\quad
R_d=\{(t,\lambda):1\le t\le5,\ 22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6,\ |\lambda|=d-t\},
\]
Pieri makes the \((t,\lambda)\)-row
\[
\bar h_t\bar s_\lambda
=\sum_{\substack{\mu\in C_d\\\mu/\lambda\text{ horizontal }t\text{-strip}}}\bar s_\mu.
\]
Thus these canonical rows have row lattice \((A_+J)_d\).

Since \(4\le|\lambda|\le30\), \(R_d=\varnothing\) for \(d\le4\) (hence \(d<4\)) and \(d>35\). For \(31\le d\le35\), \((d-30,5^6)\in R_d\), while \(C_d=\varnothing\); hence \(R_d\neq\varnothing\), but every row is the unique zero vector in \(\mathbb Z^{C_d}=0\). An omitted row family and this nonempty zero-row family have the same row lattice \(0\), but are not equal as indexed row families.

## Gaps
The supplied evidence does not give degree-\(31,\ldots,35\) row labels or \(|R_d|\times0\) matrices for artifact `a3ad933b835c991bc8edccec918dce17c0e4594e4d1d4281e32946dd7e508ece`. Therefore literal equality between the artifact’s indexed rows and the complete canonical indexed family in every degree is not established. Only the row-lattice statement and boundary classification are established algebraically.

## Next
A task-owned computation extending the stated partition-Pieri construction through degree \(35\), retaining zero-column row labels, is required to establish literal all-degree artifact-row equality.
